title: Build one million new homes
detail: Free up public and private land together with the regions and town halls. A new land law (*Ley del Suelo*) would make planning faster. Social housing could be built on land kept for public buildings (*suelo dotacional*), and offices could become affordable homes. Town halls would have 3 months to answer a building permit request, and no answer would mean yes (*silencio positivo*, "positive silence"). The programme gives no date for the million homes.
c: Spain now finishes about 100,000 homes a year. A million in four years would mean 2.5 times more, and there are not enough workers or land. The programme sets no date. Land and permits belong to the regions and town halls, so the central government can only partly speed things up.

s.t: Housing Ministry: Observatorio de Vivienda y Suelo, annual bulletin 2024 (La Moncloa)

title: Cancel the 2023 Housing Law (*Ley de Vivienda*)
detail: End the law, including its "stressed market areas" (*zonas tensionadas*) and its rent price index. The programme says the law brought more state control, more uncertainty and fewer homes to rent. It does not say what would replace the law.
c: Cancelling the law needs an ordinary law, and PP and Vox would have the votes. But regions run by PP never named stressed areas, so the effect on the market would be smaller than promised. The programme does not describe what comes next.
pos: Landlords get clear rules, and some homes may move back from short-term and tourist rentals to long-term rental.
neg: In Catalonia, where rent limits apply, tenants lose protection against big rises when they renew their contract. More homes are not certain: land and permits hold back building, not this law.

title: 4% VAT on a first home for under-40s
detail: Lower VAT (*IVA*) on a first new home from 10% to 4% for buyers under 40, paid in parts together with the mortgage. Agree with the regions a lower transfer tax (*ITP*) on second-hand first homes for young buyers. Give people 4 years, instead of the current 2, to reinvest the money from selling their main home (*vivienda habitual*) without tax.
c: A 4% rate based on age must follow the EU VAT rules. Paying VAT in parts with the mortgage is unusual, and the tax agency has no system for it. With too few homes, help for buyers mostly raises prices.
pos: A new home becomes about 6% cheaper (VAT goes from 10% to 4%), so it is easier for young people to stop renting.
neg: With too few homes, sellers keep part of the saving by asking higher prices. The state loses tax income, and the help goes to people who can already buy, not to the poorest.

s.t: Directive (EU) 2022/542 on VAT rates (BOE copy of the OJEU)
Ley 37/1992 on VAT (BOE)

title: State guarantee for the deposit
detail: Give buyers under 40 (maybe under 50 later) a public guarantee (*aval público*) for up to 20% of the price. Then the mortgage can also cover the deposit.
c: A similar guarantee from the state bank ICO for young buyers has existed since 2023, so this extends it. It is easy to do. Higher prices will take part of the help.
pos: It removes the biggest problem for young buyers: saving a 20% deposit. A similar ICO guarantee has already worked since 2023.
neg: More buyers without more homes push prices up. The state takes the risk: in a crisis, it pays when buyers cannot pay back.

s.t: Council of Ministers, 9 May 2023: ICO guarantee line for first homes (La Moncloa)

title: Squatters out within 48 hours
detail: A new law so owners get their home back within 48 hours after a court order. Owners' associations could also go to court themselves (change to the *Ley de Propiedad Horizontal*). While squatters live in the home, the owner would not pay bills or taxes, and the squatter's town-hall registration (*empadronamiento*) would not count.
c: LO 1/2025 already made squatting cases faster. Without the owner's consent, a home can be entered only with a court order or when someone is caught in the act (art. 18.2 of the Constitution). The 48 hours depends on how busy the courts are, not on the words of a law. It is realistic only with more judges.
pos: It protects owners and neighbours from people who live in a home without permission, so owners feel safer renting out homes.
neg: Vulnerable families could be wrongly evicted without a check of their situation. Courts are already too busy, so 48 hours is hard to promise. In our estimate, the effect on the housing market would be very small.

s.t: Ley Orgánica 1/2025 on the efficiency of the justice system (BOE)
Spanish Constitution, art. 18 (BOE)

title: Raise income tax bands with inflation
detail: Raise the income tax (*IRPF*) bands with inflation (*deflactar la tarifa*) and update the main allowances. Then rising prices (almost 30% in recent years, the programme says) would stop working as a hidden tax rise.
c: It makes economic sense and is technically simple. But it costs several billion euros a year, and EU budget rules limit what Spain can spend. It will more likely come step by step.
pos: It removes the hidden tax rise that inflation causes when pay rises push people into higher bands. This makes the tax fairer.
neg: People who earn more gain more euros. The state loses several billion euros a year, and the programme does not say how to replace them.

title: Income tax discount for ages 18 to 35: 100/75/50/25%
detail: Employees and self-employed people aged 18 to 35 get a discount on their first four years of income tax: 100% in the first year, then 75%, 50% and 25%. It would start with the first tax return after the law is passed.
c: It is easy to bring in by law. A discount based on age could be challenged in court as unequal treatment (arts. 14 and 31 of the Constitution). It also gives families a reason to put income in young people's names. The programme gives no cost.
pos: A strong reason for young people to work in Spain and not leave. It may bring back some who moved abroad.
neg: It is expensive and unequal: two workers with the same job pay different tax only because of their age. People could misuse it through self-employment. Nobody has shown that it stops young people from leaving.

s.t: Spanish Constitution, art. 14 (BOE)
Spanish Constitution, art. 31 (BOE)

title: 0% VAT on basic food
detail: While prices keep rising fast, 0% VAT on basic food, including meat, fish and tinned food. The programme gives no full list.
c: Spain already had 0% VAT on basic food in 2023 and 2024, and EU law allows it. Banco de España and the CNMC found that shop prices fell by almost the full cut in 2023. The Fedea think tank estimated that half of the savings went to the richest 40% of households.
pos: Cheaper food, especially for poorer households, which spend a large part of their money on food.
neg: In 2023 half of the savings went to the richest 40% of households, according to Fedea. The measure is expensive, and it is politically hard to end a tax cut later, even a temporary one.

s.t: Banco de España, Working Paper 2417 (2024): VAT cut pass-through to prices
CNMC, 10 Aug 2023: study of the VAT cut pass-through to food prices
Fedea (think tank), López Laborda et al., Apuntes 2023/02: who gained from the VAT cut

title: No social security fees for new *autónomos* in year one
detail: New self-employed workers (*autónomos*) pay no social security fee (*cuota*) in their first year. In the second year they also pay nothing if they earn less than the minimum wage (*SMI*). Their main home would be protected from creditors automatically.
c: A low fixed fee (*tarifa plana*) of €80 a month already exists. A full zero costs more and gives employers a reason to turn staff into false self-employed workers. It can be done by ordinary law.
pos: It is easier to start working for yourself, so more new businesses and more legal work.
neg: Paying less now means a smaller pension later for the self-employed person. Companies may push employees into "false self-employment".

s.t: Real Decreto-ley 13/2022: self-employed contributions and flat rate (BOE)

title: Check people who arrive without permission within 7 days, then return them fast
detail: People who cross the border without permission would be identified and checked for security within a week. Then their asylum request would be handled quickly, or they would be sent back. In emergencies the deadlines would be shorter, under the new EU system.
c: The EU Pact on Migration and Asylum, which applies from 12 June 2026, already brings checks of up to 7 days, so this promise partly just applies it. Fast returns depend on whether countries of origin agree to take their citizens back.
pos: Faster procedures, and fewer people waiting for years without a clear legal status.
neg: Seven days is short for a proper check. People with a right to asylum could be sent away, and the European Court of Human Rights could rule against Spain. Returns depend on the countries of origin.

s.t: Regulation (EU) 2024/1356 on border screening (BOE copy of the OJEU)

title: Ban mass regularisations; *arraigo* only in special cases
detail: The Immigration Law (*Ley de Extranjería*) would ban regularisations of large groups of people at once. *Arraigo* (residence based on your ties to Spain) would become a special route, decided case by case. Town-hall registration (*empadronamiento*) alone would no longer give a right to cash benefits, except in emergencies.
c: A ban on mass regularisations in the Immigration Law needs an organic law (176 votes). That is realistic with Vox. A narrower *arraigo* is easier: its rules are in the immigration regulation, which the government can change by royal decree. Permits already given cannot be taken back. A narrower *arraigo* would leave hundreds of thousands of people without papers, and there is no real way to send them away either.
pos: It shows that entering without papers does not lead to legal status, which weakens the groups that smuggle people.
neg: Hundreds of thousands of people stay without papers and work without contracts. The state gets less tax and fewer social security payments, and workers are exploited more.

s.t: Ley Orgánica 4/2000 on foreigners' rights (BOE)
Spanish Constitution, art. 81 (BOE)
Real Decreto 1155/2024, the immigration regulation (Reglamento de Extranjería) (BOE)

title: 4,500 more family doctors and better conditions for doctors
detail: At least 4,500 more doctors in local health centres (*Atención Primaria*), more training places for specialists (*MIR*), better pay and working conditions, and separate pay talks for doctors. Shorter on-call shifts (*guardias*) would come through staff planning with the regions. No date or number is given.
c: The 4,500 doctors do not exist on the job market: training a family doctor (degree plus MIR) takes many years. More MIR places help only after 2030, and the regions do the hiring.
pos: Shorter waits at local health centres. Better conditions mean fewer doctors leave to work abroad.
neg: It is expensive, and the regions run health care: the state pays but does not manage. Training doctors takes years.

title: Cancel the Amnesty Law and limit pardons
detail: Cancel the Amnesty Law (*Ley de Amnistía*), ban pardons (*indultos*) given in return for support for a government, and pass a new Pardons Law with clear rules. Corruption, terrorism and crimes against the constitutional order would be excluded.
c: The law can be cancelled (176 votes), but an amnesty that has already been applied cannot be undone: the Constitution does not allow laws that harm people for past acts (art. 9.3). In 2025 the Constitutional Court found the law mostly in line with the Constitution. A new Pardons Law is realistic.

s.t: Ley Orgánica 1/2024 on amnesty (BOE)
Spanish Constitution, art. 9 (BOE)
Constitutional Court ruling 137/2025 on the amnesty (BOE)

title: Drop the plan to close the nuclear plants
detail: Within 100 days, start the process to keep the Almaraz, Ascó, Vandellós, Cofrentes and Trillo plants open longer, with approval from the nuclear safety council (*Consejo de Seguridad Nuclear*). Rewrite the national energy and climate plan (*PNIEC*) "with realism", and support a nuclear plan that includes small modular reactors.
c: A longer life needs the owners to ask for it and a CSN report. The owners of Almaraz asked, and it can already run until June 2030 (Orden TED/864/2026). The other plants need new requests, and the companies want lower taxes.
pos: It keeps about a fifth of Spain's electricity (about 19% in 2025, according to REE) free of emissions, and gives the grid a stable supply.
neg: The owners must invest and the CSN must approve. There is still no long-term solution for nuclear waste. When there is too much power, more solar and wind power is switched off, and there is less reason to build energy storage.

s.t: Orden TED/864/2026: Almaraz extended to 8 June 2030 (BOE)
REE: 2025 year-end data, generation mix
